mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% consistently predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as it reflects accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates and supports equity valuations across all monetary regimes.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 75% of 20-day returns positive when FEDFUNDS < 4.5%
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 4.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive returns vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point increase in the unemployment rate over three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 65% of 20-day returns negative when UNRATE increases by >0.3pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances (UNRATE rise >0.3pp in 3 months).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% in one month indicate a broad-based demand contraction that reduces corporate revenue expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline > 0.5% in 1 month
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 68% of 20-day returns negative when both HOUST and RSAFS decline >0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST and RSAFS both decline >0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 0.5% in one month signals an impending manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 62% of 20-day returns negative when INDPRO declines >0.5% during late-cycle expansions
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO declines >0.5% in 1 month during late-cycle expansions.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) below 1300 thousand units signals a significant slowdown in residential construction, reducing consumer spending and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 60% of 20-day returns negative when HOUST < 1300
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1300.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% in 1 month) signal persistent inflation without monetary tightening, eroding real earnings and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% in 1 month
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 70% of 20-day returns negative when CPI>3.5% and FEDFUNDS stable
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5 and FEDFUNDS change < 0.1% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200 thousand persons signals robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 68% of 5-day returns positive when PAYEMS increase > 200k
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increase > 200k.

mechanism_narrative: In post-recession recovery phases, a 1% monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) signals accelerating consumer spending that boosts corporate revenue growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical data shows 72% of 60-day returns positive when RSAFS increases >1% during post-recession recoveries
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS increases >1% during post-recession recoveries.
